correctness.rationale: For P=z0+[0,1]u+[0,1]v with independent area-uniform X,Y, the coordinate differences xi,eta are independent triangular random variables with even moments E xi^(2j)=2/((2j+1)(2j+2)). With A=u·u>0, B=v·v>0, C=u·v and C²<AB, one has R²=A xi²+B eta²+2C xi eta. Independently expanded the polynomial with exact SymPy coefficients: M2=(A+B)/6, M4=(6A²+5AB+6B²+10C²)/90, M6=(A+B)(15A²-AB+15B²+56C²)/420, agreeing identically with RESULT.md. Setting S=A+B, p=AB/S², q=C²/S² yields precisely 0<p≤1/4 and 0≤q<p. The independent normalized-moment linear algebra gives x=12/5-14p/5+4q, y=54/7-558p/35+144q/5, inverse p=93/41-70x/41+175y/738, q=81/82-155x/164+245y/1476; all three boundary vertices were exactly confirmed. The parameter triangle maps invertibly onto triangle A=(12/5,54/7), B=(17/10,261/70), C=(27/10,153/14) with entire side AC omitted; its other two edges represent rectangles and rhombi. Reconstruction of unordered A,B and |C| is unique up to congruence; varying p between 1/7 and 1/4 with q=7p/10-1/10 yields continuum with M2=1,M4=2. On compact nondegenerate shape families, inverse of affine data is Lipschitz before taking square roots; signed-angle and equal-side degeneracies yield exact 1/2 Hölder and the transverse rectangle perturbation has moment change O(t²) but shape change O(t), proving optimality. A Monte Carlo sample in the package is corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The inverse covariogram theorem reconstructs planar convex bodies from the entire direction-labeled covariogram—much richer data than three scalar distance moments—and does NOT yield their minimal finite sufficiency. Gasparyan–Ohanyan and Martirosyan study direction-dependent random-line chord/covariogram distributions, not the independent area-uniform endpoint distance M2/M4/M6 inverse problem. Two Resultary parallelogram records were read in full: one uses projection WIDTH statistics (mean, second moment, diameter) and an angle inversion; another compares the boundary-to-interior FOURTH distance moment and angular phase transition. Neither treats the full triple of interior even moments, affine feasible triangle or 2-moment nonidentifiability. Best-of-knowledge originality therefore survives these stronger/nearby comparisons, with alias priority risk.
residual_risks: Only positive-area Euclidean parallelograms and independent area-uniform point pairs; not all quadrilaterals or boundary points.
Triangle side AC represents degenerate limits, excluded from all actual nondegenerate shapes.
Uniform Hölder statement assumes compact side and angle bounds; no finite-sample statistical guarantees.
An older probability-engineering derivation of scalar distance moments might contain an equivalent finite inverse theorem under another name.

value.rationale: The shape-from-statistics problem is a natural inverse geometric probability question. The theorem determines the entire feasible region for dimensionless observations, proves a sharp threshold of exactly three consecutive even distance moments for congruence reconstruction, supplies an explicit inverse without genericity restrictions, and gives quantitatively optimal 1/2-Hölder stability near the rectangle symmetry. These are intrinsic unknown exact invariants relevant to statistical shape retrieval, not mere formula substitution.
